extracted.intended_audience: beginner reporters, cub reporters, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide for beginners on gathering, handling, and writing news stories in a newspaper newsroom, covering organization of the paper, news values, reporting techniques, story organization, leads, sentence and paragraph craft, and specialized story types.

rubrics_metrics.name: What News Is / News Values
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines news and its values (importance of knowing the values of news, nose for news).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the essential qualities that make something news: timeliness, nearness/ localization, prominence, human interest, record-breaking or unusual events, extremes, and heroism; cultivate a 'nose for news' and understand the values so you can spot and exploit newsworthy items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in News
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be accurate in facts, names, figures, and statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify names, dates, figures, and statements; guard against rumors and falsehood; take care with lists (dead, injured, killed) and legal matters; maintain accuracy in leads and body; follow law of libel guidance when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: News must be timely — getting material into print as quickly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize speed: meet press deadlines, use devices like the fudge and advance heads for late-breaking news, file promptly via telephone/telegraph when appropriate; timeliness often determines a story's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization / Nearness of Events
rubrics_metrics.description: Localize news to make it relevant to the paper's readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring remote events home by local angles; prefer local names, effects, or consequences; use state/city editors to adapt wire copy for local interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest / Human Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and exploit human-interest elements to engage readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek pathos, humor, personality, and unusual details; use interviews and anecdotes to add human color; feature stories should foreground human interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of News / Reliability of Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a variety of dependable news sources (police blotter, courts, telegraph, correspondents, morgue, exchanges, officials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate and manage beats and correspondents; vet source reliability; maintain the morgue library; keep instructions to correspondents clear; be aware of press service and telegraph copy handling rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting the Story / Reporting Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques and duties for gathering the facts: beats, assignments, telephone, interviews, note-book and memory use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be quick and systematic: cover beats, learn to interview (questions, making people talk), take clear notes or shorthand, verify statements, use the telephone and telegraph appropriately, and follow up leads and queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of the Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange material logically (time order, space order, climactic order, complex order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the best organizational pattern for the material (summary lead with important facts first, or climactic build); maintain unity and coherence; avoid confusing complex order unless necessary for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead is the point of greatest difficulty and must be proper and effectively worded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct leads that summarize the main point (summarizing leads), are clear, concise, and interesting; know types of leads (question leads, verse leads, informal leads, suspense leads); match lead style to story type (accident, crime, feature, sports, speeches); avoid dull or ambiguous openings.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Body of the Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the lead with supporting facts, sequence, and detail in appropriate order and proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the lead with essential facts and context; maintain clearness and coherence; use proportion (emphasize most important facts); avoid repetition and unnecessary padding; use follow-ups and rewrites to sharpen the body.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph use and paragraphing rules for clarity and emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paragraphs to group related ideas; keep paragraphs focused and proportionate; use indention and paragraph marks correctly in copy; paragraphs support the sentence-level rhythm and readability of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence-level craft is governed by definite laws (length, unity, force, clarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly long or involved sentences; aim for unity of idea, clear subject-verb structures, active verbs, avoid ambiguous pronouns, and maintain rhythm and force; study sentence construction carefully to improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words / Diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose words for clarity, correctness, and effectiveness; avoid slang and trite phrases unless appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple, precise words; avoid jargon and clichés; aim for elegance and force where suitable; be mindful of word meanings and connotations; use figures of speech sparingly and correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and Usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Conform to rules of grammar (agreement, pronouns, infinitives, participles, subordination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguous pronouns, faulty agreement, split infinitives (discouraged), dangling participles; pay attention to punctuation (comma, semicolon, colon, dash, parentheses) and sentence structure to ensure clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation, Capitalization and Style Book Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the style book and proofreading marks; be consistent in punctuation and capitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided style rules (comma, semicolon, colon, hyphen, apostrophe, quotation marks, figures, abbreviations); follow the paper's style book for headlines, numbers, and special terms; use proofreader's marks correctly when submitting copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines and Slugging
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper creation of headlines and use of slugs for copy organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines that reflect the story's emphasis and fit space; use bank-man slug names and guide lines on takes; copy cutter and compositor processes require correct slugs and catch lines for assembling takes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and Condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt story length to the paper's needs; practice condensation and cutting without losing essentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to shorten copy under city editor's directions; prioritize facts and trim padding; learn to rewrite and condense while preserving meaning and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and Voice (Avoid Editorializing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an appropriate journalistic tone; avoid personal opinion in straight news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep tone objective for news stories; avoid editorializing unless writing opinion; use understatement and restraint rather than exaggeration; respect the paper's policies and editor's directions on tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and Ethical Constraints (Libel, Suppression of News)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid libel and unlawful publication; understand when news should be suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know libel law basics; avoid publishing libelous or unverified allegations; consult managing editor on risky material; follow policies on suppressing news (e.g., pending legal action, privacy, courtesy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and Quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute statements and use quotations accurately (verbatim quotes when possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear attribution for facts and quotes; prefer verbatim for important statements; avoid misleading paraphrase; put quotations in context and use quotation-marks properly; follow rules on length and placement (leads, body).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct effective interviews: preparation, questioning, making sources talk, using telephone and notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare questions in advance; use open-ended prompts to elicit details; record or take shorthand notes; get names, titles, and addresses; verify statements; know how many interviews needed and how to write up an interview-based story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized Story Types: Interviews, Speeches, Courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reporting interviews, speeches, and court proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For speeches and testimony, summarize main points in the lead and include notable verbatim quotes; for courts, be accurate with decisions and testimony; avoid editorial comment; follow procedural rules for release copies and advance stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized Story Types: Accidents and Crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reporting accidents, crimes, lists of dead/injured, and sensitive details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with names and causes; avoid publishing unverified accusations; use sensitivity for victims and families; verify official sources; construct clear accident/crime leads that summarize the essential facts without sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized Story Types: Sports
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for sports reporting: immediacy, knowledge of rules, records, and play-by-play clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish promptly (use special wires/composers for late games); be accurate in scores, plays, and rules; localize relevance (teams, players); use clear chronology or climactic order as appropriate; sporting editor may require particular style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-ups and Rewrites
rubrics_metrics.description: How to follow up initial stories and rewrite for fuller coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After initial publication, pursue follow-up facts and angles; rewrites should sharpen emphasis, correct errors, and add newly available context; know when to write a follow story and how to slug it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Stories / Human-Interest Features
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for writing feature stories and longer human-interest pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features may allow more narrative, pathos, and color; craft a strong lead that draws readers; proportion the story with anecdotes, interviews, and context; avoid dullness by choosing compelling subjects and vivid details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence Stories / Handling Correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on preparing and editing correspondence from stringers and distant reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear instructions to correspondents; edit their copy for style and accuracy; manage the space book for contributor payments; ensure state/correspondent copy is localized and meets paper standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Morgue and Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and consult archives (morgue) and exchange materials for background and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the morgue for ready biographies, past incidents, obituaries, and context; exchange editor and librarian supply material; catalog cuts and clippings for quick reference on breaking stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebook and Note-taking Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Record facts, quotations, addresses, and figures carefully at the scene or during interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a notebook consistently; write legibly, include full names, titles, and spellings; rely on notes rather than memory when possible; use shorthand if trained; review notes before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed Devices and Workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and mechanisms (fudge, autoplate, telegraph-to-compositor) to speed publication of late news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand newsroom technical devices and workflows; coordinate with telegraph and composing departments; prepare advance heads when outcome is predictable; prioritize rapid but accurate transmission of late items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy Preparation and Proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing copy (margins, longhand/typewritten, end-marks) and handling proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow copy formatting rules (margins, paragraph marks, slugs); mark inserts and changes clearly; proofread corrected copy and proofs; use proofreader marks; cooperate with copy readers and proof readers to eliminate typographical and factual errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy, Adaptability, and Following Editor's Directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral standards for working in the city room: obedience, adaptability, loyalty, and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be punctual, adaptable to city editor's style, loyal to newsroom decisions, courteous to sources and colleagues; accept rewriting and headline changes without complaint; learn newsroom policies quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Fake Stories and Rumors
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and reject fabricated or unverified stories and rumors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify suspicious accounts; cross-check with official sources; beware of 'fake stories' and unchecked rumors circulating in police blotters or public gossip; do not file until verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion and Emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate space and emphasis in a story according to importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with most important facts, give proportionate treatment to supporting details, avoid over-emphasizing trivial elements, and use boxed summaries or head placement to reflect relative importance.
